subject: Post-demo: procurement lanes, economic buyer & exception ask
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@mediwarehealth.com>, Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@mediwarehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap & ask: procurement lanes + potential exception path

Hi Sarah / Alex — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

1) Stakeholders: please confirm the economic buyer and the procurement/legal reviewers you expect to be involved. From the convo I have so far I heard: Tony Marsh (finance), Rina Patel (legal), Omar Reyes (procurement) — please correct.

2) Procurement lanes: can you sketch whether this will be handled via (A) standard PO + MSA, (B) SOW under an enterprise MSA, or (C) procurement card/pilot order? That will determine the internal steps we need to prepare for.

3) Security gating: you mentioned SOC 2 and an internal security questionnaire. If you can drop the questionnaire link or timeline, we will route it to Dev (cc’d) for review.

4) Exception ask upfront: to avoid delays we may need to request a short-term SLA variance and a modest onboarding discount if the procurement path requires custom MSA redlines. If that becomes necessary, we’d like to submit an internal exception request; Ben (cc) is our deal owner and will coordinate.

I attached a one-page pricing sheet and a procurement checklist that shows the typical docs customers ask for — helps speed things up.

Proposed next step: if you can share stakeholder names and target procurement date by EOD Monday (Nov 9), we’ll draft a mutual action plan and a provisional exception rationale to accelerate approvals.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & ask: procurement lanes + potential exception path

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side: 

- Stakeholders: Tony Marsh (SVP Finance) is the economic buyer; Rina Patel (Head of Legal) will own the contract review; Omar Reyes (Procurement Lead) manages the purchase order process. I’m the internal sponsor for the pilot.

- Procurement lane: likely route B — SOW under our enterprise MSA. We prefer to keep pilots on short SOWs but legal will need to sign off on any non-standard SLAs.

- Security: we have a short vendor security questionnaire (I attached in a separate email to you). SOC 2 Type II report will be required before production access; for pilot we can accept an interim security attestation if you provide relevant controls evidence.

- Timeline: procurement kickoff targeting week of Nov 22, contracting through Dec. We’d like to run a four-week pilot in Jan depending on contract timing.

If you anticipate needing an SLA or pricing exception, please send the justification and proposed durations so we can preview with finance/legal.

I’ll share the questionnaire and the initial stakeholder contact list by EOD.

Best,
Sarah Nguyen
Director, AI/ML Programs
MediWare Health

Laura — forwarding the thread with MediWare. They’ve outlined a SOW-under-MSA route and will need SOC 2 evidence for prod; pilot may accept attestation. Procurement kickoff targeted week of Nov 22 which compresses our legal turnaround.

Ask: can we provisionally approve a limited discount and an SLA variance for pilot customers who: (a) run a 4-week paid pilot, (b) sign a short SOW and accept baseline fallback routing, and (c) complete security attestation within 2 weeks?

Proposed exception details: 
- 10% onboarding discount for first 3 months (applies to pilot billing only)
- SLA: allow 12-hour response time for non-prod incidents (vs. standard 4-hour) during pilot; prod must meet our standard SLA
- Conditionality: exception expires automatically if we proceed to production without a signed production SOW that adopts standard SLA/pricing

I attached the internal exception_request_form.pdf and a short rationale we’d present to Legal/Finance. If you’re ok with provisional terms, I’ll escalate formally to finance and loop in Legal for any MSA redlines.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap & ask: procurement lanes + potential exception path

Thanks Ben — provisional approval granted with guardrails.

Decision: Approve a time-boxed exception to accelerate the MediWare pilot under the following conditions:
1) Discount capped at 10% for a maximum of 3 months, applied to pilot invoices only.
2) Temporary SLA relaxation to 12-hour response for non-prod incidents during pilot; production must adhere to standard SLA if/when prod is purchased.
3) Dev will perform a rapid security attestation review within 5 business days; SOC 2 Type II must be provided before production access.
4) Legal to review any MSA redlines; no permanent MSA modifications without General Counsel sign-off.
5) Exception formally documented and timestamped in our internal approvals system; Ben to file the exception_request_form and assign a finance approver.

Ben/Marcus — please prepare a one-page exception summary (rationale, duration, KPIs, rollback plan) and drop it into the approvals queue. Dev, please confirm availability for the attestation review.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
